input.quote: (a) Title to all know-how, inventions and other intellectual property made solely by Ono personnel (or that of any Affiliate) in connection with this Agreement shall be owned by Ono (or its respective Affiliate).
input.rationale: The IP allocation works in our favour and no Ono IP or data is assigned to Array during the term. Section 11.1(a) gives Ono outright ownership of everything made solely by Ono personnel (Array's ownership of its own compound IP under 11.1(b) is the acceptable "vendor keeps its platform" position), Section 4.6(c) (p0329) confirms Ono owns its INDs and Marketing Approvals in the Ono Territory, Section 2.7 preserves each Party's retained rights, and Section 13.1 converts our Article II licences into perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, royalty-free, sublicensable licences on expiry — which independently satisfies the fallback licence-back requirement. The outbound Grant-Back in Section 2.6 is a non-exclusive, subject-to-our-exclusivity licence of Improvements and our Joint IP interest, not an assignment, so it is not walk-away territory. Two points sit at the fallback rather than the preferred position and are noted rather than redlined: (i) Section 11.1(c) does create joint ownership of jointly-made IP, and 11.1(d) limits each Party to internal practice and requires the other Party's consent to enforce, license or assign — but the restriction is reciprocal and expressly disapplied "to the extent any jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property are included in subject matter licensed by one Party to the other", and our Section 2.1(a)-(c) licences cover Array's interests in the Joint Patents and Joint Know-How for Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products throughout the Ono Territory, so we retain a workable right to exploit joint IP across our whole commercial field; (ii) Sections 14.2(a)(iii) and (vii) require assignment of Product-specific Regulatory Filings and Product Trademarks on termination, but that is ordinary reversion of a licensed product (our corporate names are carved out) and, where we terminate for Array's material breach or insolvency under 13.3/13.4, Section 14.2(a)(ix) requires Array to pay market-rate consideration for those rights instead. No redline warranted.
